issues.body: `_workflow_job_key` still bounds the job with `(?=^  \S|\Z)`. A two-space comment satisfies that lookahead even though YAML ignores comment-only lines for mapping structure. Placing `  # keepalive controls` after the captured `    runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and before `    if: false` truncates the block: `runs-on` supplies the positive control, while `if` incorrectly reads as absent, so the live row stays green although GitHub disables the job. The updated `synthetic_job` contains only `    # if: ...`, a four-space comment, and still does not test the round-4 boundary case.
issues.fix_hint: Make job-boundary detection skip comment-only lines while still refusing missing or ambiguous job definitions. Add the exact independent regression fixture: a two-space comment between `    runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and `    if: false`, and assert that the gate is still returned while the positive control occurs before the comment.
issues.title: A job-indented comment still hides subsequent job gates

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major remains unchanged. `_workflow_job_key` still terminates the selected job at `(?=^  \S|\Z)`, so a valid two-space comment is mistaken for the next job boundary. The revised `synthetic_job` still places its comment at four spaces inside the job and does not exercise the reported bypass. With `  # keepalive controls` after `    runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and before `    if: false`, the extractor retains the positive control but truncates away the disabling gate; the production assertion therefore stays green while GitHub skips the job. Because the same soundness defect remains at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
